bull_bear.body: Diversified lender base (added India + local South-Africa lines; lead bank raised limits; +INR3,200 cr fresh lines). Term loans repay this year & next → "almost deleveraged" on fund-based after. Negative-WC discipline maintained. Regular dividend intent flagged; growth funded off customer advances not equity.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Execution ramp / H2 back-ended** — the entire guide rests on Q3-Q4; any further LOA slippage repeats Q1.
- **Litigation overhang:** total claims ~INR1,800 cr; 2 US project claims in court (2-3 yrs); Australia arbitration ~INR200 cr (INR110 cr under promoter LD-indemnity); ~INR800 cr receivables indemnity-covered (INR120-130 cr expected this year); ~INR3,800 cr contingent "frivolous" claims (no cash-out expected). BG invocation risk on delayed orders is nil (contract dates not yet started).
- **DCR/module-price & BESS-localization** policy uncertainty on future bids (locked on current orders).
- **Reliance timing/quantum** entirely on Reliance's rollout schedule.
- Domestic ordering slow for a 2nd straight quarter.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Candid on the miss ("assumptions were on track… unfortunately all new orders' LOAs delayed"), disciplined on not chasing aggressive bids, and blunt on the H2 pressure ("Boss, we have no option… we have to perform"). CFO detailed and consistent on claims/indemnity mechanics. Reliance answers appropriately guarded (arm's-length, terms open). Tone = confident-but-accountable; execution is the credibility test next two quarters.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The revenue miss is a timing artefact, not demand loss** — existing UOV was late-stage (supplies already booked) and new orders slipped LOA; H2 mechanically re-loads.
- **Reliance optionality sits entirely outside the 10-15% guide** — any Kutch orders are upside, but on Reliance's clock; likely majority free-issue supply, arm's-length.
- **DCR is the swing factor for the sector** — SWSOLAR locked Coal India prices, so it is comparatively insulated vs peers exposed to the module-price upsurge; watch it as the first DCR-model proof point.
- O&M is quietly inflecting to a INR400-450 cr, ~20%-GM annuity — a stabilising counterweight to lumpy EPC.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Strong Balance Sheet" markers as of June 2026: Net worth INR 709 cr, Net D/E 0.9x and a BBB+ credit rating.
- "Bank borrowings has decreased by ~INR 129 cr versus last quarter due to scheduled repayments done" — gross debt of 1,035 (Jun-26) versus 1,164 (Mar-26); "Debt levels remain stable and term debt continues to decrease with repayments".
- Net working capital "continues to remain negative at INR 260 crore as of Jun 2026" (versus -329 at Q4FY26 and -348 at Q1FY26); receivable days 161 (Jun-26) versus 138 (Mar-26) and payable days 157 versus 135.
- Raised INR 1,500 crore through the QIP route in 2024.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strong in-house design and engineering talent pool delivering customised solutions
- Cost-competitive execution leveraging a low-cost India base for global delivery
- One of the only global pure-play solar EPC players with significant presence and operational experience across geographies
- Bankable player with strong customer relationships driving high retention and repeat business, evidenced by a strong track record executing complex, large-scale EPC projects
- Quick decision-making and well-defined internal processes enabling timely execution
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body: - Geographic revenue concentration in India — The Directors' Report states the Company's core operations are currently focused on the domestic Indian market, with international operations conducted only through global subsidiaries and branch offices; a downturn in Indian solar EPC demand or policy would disproportionately affect the business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **International EPC:** 4 projects (South Africa, Spain, Italy) at completion "within/above targeted margins"; 3 new won (2 South Africa + 1 Egypt) start execution ~this quarter. Nigeria slow (elections) — no FY27 revenue assumed.
- **O&M:** record **18.3 GW** peak (from 13.5 GW) — fed by own EPC completions (5.8 GW DC commissioned last year) + third-party (1.2 GW single order). Steady annuity, low overhead, ~20% GM.
- **BESS:** executing 1 project (battery client-supplied, free-issue → no duty/regulatory margin risk currently); future turnkey BESS margins ~PV-BoS (~10%), battery portion can be thinner/turbulent. Sourcing cautious — Indian "Make-in-India" battery market immature (assembly only); evaluating partners.
- **Floating solar:** executing India's largest with NTPC-DVC (Tilaiya, Jharkhand); more NTPC-DVC + state tenders coming.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Execution/scale credibility:** ~28 GW executed globally; 4 international projects delivered at/above target margins — the basis for the Egypt/marquee-developer wins and rising ticket sizes.
- **Negative working-capital + back-to-back procurement** model: customer advances + supplier LCs (90-180 days) fund growth; management frames conservatism as the durability edge as the cycle matures.
- **O&M stickiness:** customers migrate O&M to SWSOLAR after seeing plant performance — annuity moat.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Limited is a global provider of renewable energy engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) solutions serving the solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and wind segments, primarily delivering EPC services for utility-scale solar and hybrid power projects with capabilities spanning concept development through commissioning. The Company also offers operations and maintenance (O&M) services, including for projects developed by third parties, and while core operations are currently focused on the domestic Indian market, it conducts international operations through global subsidiaries and branch offices targeting geographies with favorable solar policies and high solar resource potential.

- **O&M:** Solar, wind, storage and hybrid asset O&M, Centralised monitoring platform, Drone thermography, IV curve diagnostics, Robotic and mechanised cleaning, AI-driven predictive analytics

latest_quarter.body: EPC GM guided **8-10%** (mix-dependent: turnkey low-%/high-absolute, BoS ~10%); DCR module-price shock largely hedged on Coal India (price locked). Overheads flat in absolute terms, falling as % on growth → operating leverage in H2. O&M GM ~20%. Forex helped reported EBITDA this quarter.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** Revenue INR1,590 cr (-10% YoY, down QoQ) on delayed LOAs/late-stage UOV; GM 9.9%; operational EBITDA INR78 cr (4.9%); reported EBITDA INR96 cr (forex); PAT INR53 cr (+36%). **Record UOV INR13,000 cr** after USD560 m Egypt win (1,000 MW + 600 MWh BESS, 50-50 JV). O&M 18.3 GW (+40% YoY rev). WC -INR260 cr. Guide trimmed to **10-15% FY27 (ex-Reliance)**; Q2 soft, H2 heavy (Q4 >INR2,500 cr). O&M INR400-450 cr FY27. Egypt NTP Sept-26 → rev Q4FY27. Coal India DCR orders price-locked, LOA pending.
- _next → check: Q2 revenue (mgmt flags soft) then H2 ramp to ~INR2,500-3,000 cr/qtr; Egypt NTP by Sept; Coal India + Reliance LOAs landing; O&M rev toward INR400-450 cr from Q3; UOV >INR10,000 cr at FY27-end; indemnity realisation INR120-130 cr; DCR-model margin outcome._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27: 10-15%** (ex-Reliance) — trimmed from ">15%" last quarter; high FY26 base.
- **Cadence:** Q2 also soft (~Q1 range); **H2 heavy — Q4 target >INR2,500 cr**, potentially ~INR3,000 cr; H2 execution must exceed H1 materially.
- **EPC gross margin: 8-10%** (turnkey lower % but higher absolute; BoS ~10%); marginal EBITDA-margin impact, offset by operating leverage.
- **O&M: revenue INR400-450 cr FY27** (vs INR268 cr FY26); gross margin **~20%** stabilised; full 18.3 GW contributes **from Q3FY27**.
- **Order book/UOV: >INR10,000 cr at FY27-end**; order-inflow growth **10-15%** over last year.
- **Egypt:** NTP expected **Sept-2026**, 13-15 month build → revenue contribution from **Q4FY27**.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **UOV INR13,000 cr** (record). 6 turnkey projects (3 India + 3 international) worth ~INR9,000 cr **yet to start** — meaningful contribution H2FY27; large-project advances should improve WC.
- **Egypt West Minya:** 1,000 MW AC solar + 600 MWh BESS, ~USD560 m, 50-50 JV with Hassan Allam Construction — full EPC scope (PV, battery, grid/transmission, BoP).
- **Bid pipeline 27.7 GW, ~90% India** (solar PV + BESS); management sees **INR45,000-50,000 cr** of orders in Q3-Q4 (~25 GW utility + 35 GWh BESS). BESS ordering value expected ~equal to PV over time.
- This quarter industry orders concluded only **INR6,400 cr** (SWSOLAR expected >INR20,000 cr) — deferred by DCR/module-price uncertainty; SWSOLAR stayed patient/margin-selective, deliberately not chasing aggressive bids.
- **Coal India** orders (L1, **DCR category, price locked**) awaiting LOA — first DCR-model demonstration; Reliance order LOA also delayed.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Reliance New Energy (Kutch RE hub):** 5.5-lakh-acre RTC ambition, 40 GWh battery Gigafactory (→120 GWh pathway) commissioning this year; SWSOLAR working on technical config/execution readiness, "confident of a large share" — **arm's-length, terms not closed** (upside not in the 10-15% guide).
- BESS is the structural second leg (Govt 500 MW-by-2030 target; 35-40 GWh opportunity over 2-3 yrs).
- O&M CAGR to compound (adding ~4-5 GW/yr own + ~2 GW third-party).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Disciplined, market-specific international expansion strategy focused on geographies with favorable solar power policies and high solar resource potential, designed to strengthen bidding capabilities and competitiveness in each target geography
- Diversification into adjacent high-growth segments — wind EPC, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and hybrid solutions — to become a holistic energy transition partner offering integrated, round-the-clock renewable energy solutions
- Growing the Operations & Maintenance (O&M) franchise as a key differentiator, providing stable, annuity-like revenues via own EPC project commissioning plus third-party portfolio acquisitions
- Prioritising risk-adjusted returns over volume in international bidding, with Africa, Middle East and Europe as priority overseas markets
- Sustained investment in project management infrastructure — centralised command-and-control systems, standardised construction methodologies, and digitised project delivery workflows — to scale execution discipline
- Deliberate scaling of the global workforce and engineering/procurement bench in anticipation of a growing pipeline of GW-scale projects
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SWREL's expansion during FY 2026 was execution-led rather than manufacturing-capex led: it commissioned approximately 4.5 GW AC (~5.9 GW DC) of solar capacity across multiple projects in India and overseas, expanding its cumulative global EPC portfolio to 27.3 GWp across 20 countries and its O&M portfolio to 13.5 GWp (up from 8.7 GW, a 50% Y-o-Y surge). In India it is simultaneously executing over 5.5 GWp across 8 projects in the Khavda, Gujarat cluster (5 for NTPC, 2 for GIPCL, 1 for Engie), and the Tilaiya Floating Solar Project (155 MW) at the Tilaiya Dam in Jharkhand is under development. The Company ventured into wind EPC in April 2025 and secured a 790 MWh BESS plant in Rajasthan, extending its footprint into adjacent renewable verticals (wind, BESS, hybrid) alongside its core solar EPC and O&M business. International presence spans offices in 28 countries with projects executed in 20, and the Company continues a disciplined, market-specific approach to entering new geographies with favourable solar policy and resource potential.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's renewable energy ambitions are accelerating and the global solar market is expanding, positioning the Company to capitalise on demand
- Management anticipates a very large domestic client starting execution of its multi-year, multi-GW renewables roll-out this fiscal (FY 2027)
- The BESS market in India is expected to see strong/exponential growth from this year as emphasis on battery storage gains prominence
- A significant proportion of new order wins came from repeat clients, seen as a driver of continued order inflow and evidence of execution trust
- Management is monitoring solar module price dynamics closely but is satisfied the existing order book carries adequate contractual protection against near-term commodity risk
- International (post-COVID) projects in Africa and Europe have been executed at margins that are attractive and, in several cases, superior to domestic benchmarks, supporting continued disciplined international growth
- O&M gross margins are stabilising at approximately 20%, with further portfolio additions expected to make O&M an increasingly important contributor to earnings quality
- New order inflows reached INR 10,062 crore in FY 2026, a 43% Y-o-Y growth across 12 projects, exceeding the 15% growth management had conservatively projected at the start of the fiscal year
- Unexecuted Order Value (UOV) stood at INR 11,813 crore entering FY 2027, the highest since the COVID period, providing revenue visibility
- Domestic order inflows were INR 7,659 crore across 10 projects totalling approximately 4.8 GW DC
- International orders included two projects from South Africa worth approximately USD 270 million
- Domestic EPC Unexecuted Order Value stands at INR 9,251 crore, providing revenue visibility for the year ahead
- Bid pipeline of approximately 31 GW as the Company enters FY 2027, of which over 88% is in India
- The Company has been declared the lowest bidder for a major 1.2 GW DC turnkey project from Coal India, which on conversion would represent a landmark public sector mandate
- O&M portfolio surged 50% Y-o-Y from 8.7 GW to 13.5 GW, achieved via own EPC commissioning and third-party portfolio acquisitions
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A weak top-line quarter by design — revenue **-10% YoY to INR1,590 cr** as new orders' LOAs/NTPs slipped and existing UOV was already late-stage — but the order book tells the real story: **record UOV INR13,000 cr** after the landmark **USD560 m Egypt** win (1,000 MW solar + 600 MWh BESS, 50-50 JV), the third GW-scale order in nine months. Management holds a **10-15% FY27 revenue growth** guide (ex-Reliance) but concedes Q2 stays soft and **H2 must carry ~INR2,500-3,000 cr/quarter** execution — the key show-me. Negative working capital preserved (-INR260 cr); O&M inflecting (18.3 GW, +40% YoY).
